snapshot.title: TNPSC Polity: Making of Constitution & Preamble
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Polity Hook: M.N. Roy: 1934. Ambedkar: Drafting. 8th Sch: Languages. 42nd: Socialist/Secular. USA: FR. UK: Parliament.

quick_notes.title: Making of Constitution
quick_notes.detail: 1st proposed by M.N. Roy (1934). Constituent Assembly formed under Cabinet Mission (1946). Chairman : Rajendra Prasad. Drafting Head : B.R. Ambedkar.
quick_notes.explanation: The Constitution of India was first proposed in 1934 by M.N. Roy, who suggested that Indians should write their own governing rules. Later, in 1946, a special group called the Constituent Assembly (the body of elected members who would write the constitution) was formed because of the Cabinet Mission, which was a British government plan to help India create its own government. The Assembly had a Chairman named Rajendra Prasad, who led the overall meetings. The person in charge of the Drafting Committee, the group that actually wrote the constitution's text, was B.R. Ambedkar, who is called the Drafting Head.

quick_notes.title: Borrowed Features
quick_notes.detail: USA (FR, Preamble). UK (Parliamentary). Ireland (DPSP). USSR (Duties). South Africa (Amendment).
quick_notes.explanation: The Indian Constitution was created by studying the constitutions of other countries and taking their best ideas. From the United States of America (USA), India borrowed the concept of Fundamental Rights (FR), which are basic human rights guaranteed to all citizens, and the Preamble, which is the introductory statement that explains the Constitution's goals. From the United Kingdom (UK), India adopted the Parliamentary system, meaning the government is run by a Prime Minister and a Cabinet who are members of the Parliament (the law-making body). From Ireland, India took the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for the government to create laws that ensure social and economic justice for the people. From the former Soviet Union (USSR), India borrowed the idea of Fundamental Duties, which are the basic obligations every citizen must follow, such as respecting the national flag. Finally, from South Africa, India adopted the method for amending the Constitution, which is the formal process of changing or adding to the Constitution's text.

quick_notes.title: The Preamble
quick_notes.detail: "Identity Card" of the Constitution (N.A. Palkhivala). Objectives Resolution (Nehru). 42nd Amend added "Socialist, Secular, Integrity".
quick_notes.explanation: The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution of India, often called its "Identity Card" by the lawyer N.A. Palkhivala because it summarizes the Constitution's philosophy and goals. It was based on the Objectives Resolution, a document drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946 that laid down the core principles for India's independent constitution. Originally, the Preamble described India as a "Sovereign Democratic Republic." Later, the 42nd Amendment, passed in 1976, added the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" to the Preamble, so it now reads "Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic" and includes "unity and integrity of the Nation." "Socialist" means the government works to reduce economic inequality, "Secular" means the state treats all religions equally, and "Integrity" means the nation's unity cannot be broken. The Preamble is not legally enforceable in court but is used by judges to interpret the meaning of other parts of the Constitution.

quick_notes.title: Schedules (12)
quick_notes.explanation: The Indian Constitution has 12 schedules, which are lists that add detailed rules to the main articles. Schedule 1 lists the names and territories of all States and Union Territories (UTs), which are administrative regions directly governed by the central government. Schedule 3 provides the exact wording of oaths and affirmations that officials like the President and judges must take before assuming office. Schedule 4 allocates how many seats each state gets in the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of Parliament. Schedule 8 recognizes 22 official languages of India, such as Hindi, Tamil, and Bengali. Schedule 10 contains the anti-defection law, which sets rules to stop elected members from switching their political party after being elected, and Schedule 11 lists the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats, which are local self-government bodies in villages.

quick_notes.title: Salient Features
quick_notes.detail: Lengthiest written constitution. Secular state. Single citizenship. Independent Judiciary.
quick_notes.explanation: The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world, meaning it is a single document that contains all the fundamental laws of the country and is much larger than any other nation's constitution. India is a secular state, which means the government does not have an official religion and treats all religions equally without favoring or discriminating against any. The constitution provides for single citizenship, so every Indian is a citizen of India only, not of any separate state, and has the same rights and duties regardless of which state they live in. It also establishes an independent judiciary, meaning the court system, especially the Supreme Court, is free from control by the legislative or executive
